{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# CMatrix

Matrix-like effect in your terminal

## Overview

CMatrix is based on the screensaver from The Matrix website. It shows text
flying in and out in a terminal like as seen in "The Matrix" movie. It can
scroll lines all at the same rate or asynchronously and at a user-defined
speed.

CMatrix is inspired from 'The Matrix' movie.

> Disclaimer: We are in no way affiliated with the movie "The Matrix", "Warner Bros" nor
any of its affiliates in any way, just fans.

## Usage

Run CMatrix with the following command:
```sh
cmatrix
```

Run with different arguments to get different effects:
```sh
cmatrix [-abBflohnsmVx] [-u update] [-C color]
```

Example:
```sh
cmatrix -ba -u 2 -C red
```

### Command-line Options

- `-a` - Asynchronous scroll
- `-b` - Bold characters on
- `-B` - All bold characters (overrides -b)
- `-f` - Force the linux $TERM type to be on
- `-l` - Linux mode (sets "matrix.fnt" font in console)
- `-o` - Use old-style scrolling
- `-c` - Only print the shadows of letters
- `-L` - Locks cmatrix, unable to quit
- `-h, -?` - Print usage and exit
- `-r` - "Rainbow" mode, rainbow colored characters
- `-k` - Every characters change
- `-n` - No bold characters (overrides -b and -B)
- `-s` - "Screensaver" mode, exits on first keystroke
- `-m` - "Lambda" mode, every character becomes a lambda
- `-x` - X window mode
- `-V` - Print version information and exit
- `-u delay` - Screen update delay 0-9, default 4
- `-C color` - Use this color for matrix (default green). Valid colors are green, red, blue, white, yellow, cyan, magenta and black.
- `-M message` - Add a message in the center of cmatrix
- `-t tty` - Set tty to use

### Interactive Keystrokes

The following keystrokes are available during execution (unavailable in -s mode):

- `a` - Toggle asynchronous scroll
- `b` - Random bold characters
- `B` - All bold characters
- `n` - Turn off bold characters
- `0-9` - Adjust update speed
- `! @ # $ % ^ & )` - Change the color of the matrix:
  - `!` - red
  - `@` - green
  - `#` - yellow
  - `$` - blue
  - `%` - magenta
  - `^` - cyan
  - `&` - white
  - `)` - black
- `q` - Quit the program

### Tips

- To get the program to look most like the movie, use: `cmatrix -lba`
- To get the program to look most like the Win/Mac screensaver, use: `cmatrix -ol`

Note: cmatrix is probably not particularly portable or efficient, but it won't hog
too much CPU time.

## Screenshots

![cmatrix screenshot](./data/img/capture_bold_font.png)

## Screencasts

![cmatrix screencast](./data/img/capture_orig.gif)

## License

This software is provided under the GNU GPL v3. [View License](./COPYING)
"
}

def parse_args(args):
    """Parse command line arguments"""
    options = {
        'a': False,      # Asynchronous scroll
        'b': False,      # Bold characters on
        'B': False,      # All bold characters
        'c': False,      # Use Japanese characters
        'f': False,      # Force linux TERM
        'l': False,      # Linux mode
        'L': False,      # Lock mode
        'o': False,      # Old-style scrolling
        'n': False,      # No bold characters
        's': False,      # Screensaver mode
        'x': False,      # X window mode
        'r': False,      # Rainbow mode
        'm': False,      # Lambda mode
        'k': False,      # Characters change
        'u': 4,          # Update delay
        'C': 'green',    # Color
        't': None,       # TTY
        'M': None,       # Message
        'h': False,      # Help
        'V': False,      # Version
        'q': False,      # Quit
    }
    
    i = 0
    while i < len(args):
        arg = args[i]
        if arg in ['-h', '-?']:
            options['h'] = True
            i += 1
        elif arg == '-V':
            options['V'] = True
            i += 1
        elif arg == '-a':
            options['a'] = True
            i += 1
        elif arg == '-b':
            options['b'] = True
            i += 1
        elif arg == '-B':
            options['B'] = True
            i += 1
        elif arg == '-c':
            options['c'] = True
            i += 1
        elif arg == '-f':
            options['f'] = True
            i += 1
        elif arg == '-l':
            options['l'] = True
            i += 1
        elif arg == '-L':
            options['L'] = True
            i += 1
        elif arg == '-o':
            options['o'] = True
            i += 1
        elif arg == '-n':
            options['n'] = True
            i += 1
        elif arg == '-s':
            options['s'] = True
            i += 1
        elif arg == '-x':
            options['x'] = True
            i += 1
        elif arg == '-r':
            options['r'] = True
            i += 1
        elif arg == '-m':
            options['m'] = True
            i += 1
        elif arg == '-k':
            options['k'] = True
            i += 1
        elif arg == '-u':
            if i + 1 < len(args):
                try:
                    options['u'] = int(args[i + 1])
                    if options['u'] < 0 or options['u'] > 10:
                        print("Error opening terminal: unknown.")
                        sys.exit(1)
                except ValueError:
                    print("Error opening terminal: unknown.")
                    sys.exit(1)
                i += 2
            else:
                print("Error opening terminal: unknown.")
                sys.exit(1)
        elif arg == '-C':
            if i + 1 < len(args):
                options['C'] = args[i + 1].lower()
                if options['C'] not in VALID_COLORS:
                    print(" Invalid color selection")
                    print(" Valid colors are green, red, blue, white, yellow, cyan, magenta and black.")
                i += 2
            else:
                print("Error opening terminal: unknown.")
                sys.exit(1)
        elif arg == '-t':
            if i + 1 < len(args):
                options['t'] = args[i + 1]
                i += 2
            else:
                print("Error opening terminal: unknown.")
                sys.exit(1)
        elif arg == '-M':
            if i + 1 < len(args):
                options['M'] = args[i + 1]
                i += 2
            else:
                print("Error opening terminal: unknown.")
                sys.exit(1)
        else:
            print(" Usage: cmatrix -[abBcfhlsmVxk] [-u delay] [-C color] [-t tty] [-M message]")
            print(" -a: Asynchronous scroll")
            print(" -b: Bold characters on")
            print(" -B: All bold characters (overrides -b)")
            print(" -c: Use Japanese characters as seen in the original matrix. Requires appropriate fonts")
            print(" -f: Force the linux $TERM type to be on")
            print(" -l: Linux mode (uses matrix console font)")
            print(" -L: Lock mode (can be closed from another terminal)")
            print(" -o: Use old-style scrolling")
            print(" -h: Print usage and exit")
            print(" -n: No bold characters (overrides -b and -B, default)")
            print(" -s: \"Screensaver\" mode, exits on first keystroke")
            print(" -x: X window mode, use if your xterm is using mtx.pcf")
            print(" -V: Print version information and exit")
            print(" -M [message]: Prints your message in the center of the screen. Overrides -L's default message.")
            print(" -u delay (0 - 10, default 4): Screen update delay")
            print(" -C [color]: Use this color for matrix (default green)")
            print(" -r: rainbow mode")
            print(" -m: lambda mode")
            print(" -k: Characters change while scrolling. (Works without -o opt.)")
            print(" -t [tty]: Set tty to use")
            sys.exit(0)
    
    return options

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# CMatrix

Matrix-like effect in your terminal

## Overview

CMatrix is based on the screensaver from The Matrix website. It shows text
flying in and out in a terminal like as seen in "The Matrix" movie. It can
scroll lines all at the same rate or asynchronously and at a user-defined
speed.

CMatrix is inspired from 'The Matrix' movie.

> Disclaimer: We are in no way affiliated with the movie "The Matrix", "Warner Bros" nor
any of its affiliates in any way, just fans.

## Usage

Run CMatrix with the following command:
```sh
cmatrix
```

Run with different arguments to get different effects:
```sh
cmatrix [-abBflohnsmVx] [-u update] [-C color]
```

Example:
```sh
cmatrix -ba -u 2 -C red
```

### Command-line Options

- `-a` - Asynchronous scroll
- `-b` - Bold characters on
- `-B` - All bold characters (overrides -b)
- `-f` - Force the linux $TERM type to be on
- `-l` - Linux mode (sets "matrix.fnt" font in console)
- `-o` - Use old-style scrolling
- `-c` - Only print the shadows of letters
- `-L` - Locks cmatrix, unable to quit
- `-h, -?` - Print usage and exit
- `-r` - "Rainbow" mode, rainbow colored characters
- `-k` - Every characters change
- `-n` - No bold characters (overrides -b and -B)
- `-s` - "Screensaver" mode, exits on first keystroke
- `-m` - "Lambda" mode, every character becomes a lambda
- `-x` - X window mode
- `-V` - Print version information and exit
- `-u delay` - Screen update delay 0-9, default 4
- `-C color` - Use this color for matrix (default green). Valid colors are green, red, blue, white, yellow, cyan, magenta and black.
- `-M message` - Add a message in the center of cmatrix
- `-t tty` - Set tty to use

### Interactive Keystrokes

The following keystrokes are available during execution (unavailable in -s mode):

- `a` - Toggle asynchronous scroll
- `b` - Random bold characters
- `B` - All bold characters
- `n` - Turn off bold characters
- `0-9` - Adjust update speed
- `! @ # $ % ^ & )` - Change the color of the matrix:
  - `!` - red
  - `@` - green
  - `#` - yellow
  - `$` - blue
  - `%` - magenta
  - `^` - cyan
  - `&` - white
  - `)` - black
- `q` - Quit the program

### Tips

- To get the program to look most like the movie, use: `cmatrix -lba`
- To get the program to look most like the Win/Mac screensaver, use: `cmatrix -ol`

Note: cmatrix is probably not particularly portable or efficient, but it won't hog
too much CPU time.

## Screenshots

![cmatrix screenshot](./data/img/capture_bold_font.png)

## Screencasts

![cmatrix screencast](./data/img/capture_orig.gif)

## License

This software is provided under the GNU GPL v3. [View License](./COPYING)
"

Matrix-like effect in your terminal

## Overview

CMatrix is based on the screensaver from The Matrix website. It shows text
flying in and out in a terminal like as seen in "The Matrix" movie. It can
scroll lines all at the same rate or asynchronously and at a user-defined
speed.

CMatrix is inspired from 'The Matrix' movie.

> Disclaimer: We are in no way affiliated with the movie "The Matrix", "Warner Bros" nor
any of its affiliates in any way, just fans.

## Usage

Run CMatrix with the following command:
```sh
cmatrix
```

Run with different arguments to get different effects:
```sh
cmatrix [-abBflohnsmVx] [-u update] [-C color]
```

Example:
```sh
cmatrix -ba -u 2 -C red
```

### Command-line Options

- `-a` - Asynchronous scroll
- `-b` - Bold characters on
- `-B` - All bold characters (overrides -b)
- `-f` - Force the linux $TERM type to be on
- `-l` - Linux mode (sets "matrix.fnt" font in console)
- `-o` - Use old-style scrolling
- `-c` - Only print the shadows of letters
- `-L` - Locks cmatrix, unable to quit
- `-h, -?` - Print usage and exit
- `-r` - "Rainbow" mode, rainbow colored characters
- `-k` - Every characters change
- `-n` - No bold characters (overrides -b and -B)
- `-s` - "Screensaver" mode, exits on first keystroke
- `-m` - "Lambda" mode, every character becomes a lambda
- `-x` - X window mode
- `-V` - Print version information and exit
- `-u delay` - Screen update delay 0-9, default 4
- `-C color` - Use this color for matrix (default green). Valid colors are green, red, blue, white, yellow, cyan, magenta and black.
- `-M message` - Add a message in the center of cmatrix
- `-t tty` - Set tty to use

### Interactive Keystrokes

The following keystrokes are available during execution (unavailable in -s mode):

- `a` - Toggle asynchronous scroll
- `b` - Random bold characters
- `B` - All bold characters
- `n` - Turn off bold characters
- `0-9` - Adjust update speed
- `! @ # $ % ^ & )` - Change the color of the matrix:
  - `!` - red
  - `@` - green
  - `#` - yellow
  - `$` - blue
  - `%` - magenta
  - `^` - cyan
  - `&` - white
  - `)` - black
- `q` - Quit the program

### Tips

- To get the program to look most like the movie, use: `cmatrix -lba`
- To get the program to look most like the Win/Mac screensaver, use: `cmatrix -ol`

Note: cmatrix is probably not particularly portable or efficient, but it won't hog

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# CMatrix

Matrix-like effect in your terminal

## Overview

CMatrix is based on the screensaver from The Matrix website. It shows text
flying in and out in a terminal like as seen in "The Matrix" movie. It can
scroll lines all at the same rate or asynchronously and at a user-defined
speed.

CMatrix is inspired from 'The Matrix' movie.

> Disclaimer: We are in no way affiliated with the movie "The Matrix", "Warner Bros" nor
any of its affiliates in any way, just fans.

## Usage

Run CMatrix with the following command:
```sh
cmatrix
```

Run with different arguments to get different effects:
```sh
cmatrix [-abBflohnsmVx] [-u update] [-C color]
```

Example:
```sh
cmatrix -ba -u 2 -C red
```

### Command-line Options

- `-a` - Asynchronous scroll
- `-b` - Bold characters on
- `-B` - All bold characters (overrides -b)
- `-f` - Force the linux $TERM type to be on
- `-l` - Linux mode (sets "matrix.fnt" font in console)
- `-o` - Use old-style scrolling
- `-c` - Only print the shadows of letters
- `-L` - Locks cmatrix, unable to quit
- `-h, -?` - Print usage and exit
- `-r` - "Rainbow" mode, rainbow colored characters
- `-k` - Every characters change
- `-n` - No bold characters (overrides -b and -B)
- `-s` - "Screensaver" mode, exits on first keystroke
- `-m` - "Lambda" mode, every character becomes a lambda
- `-x` - X window mode
- `-V` - Print version information and exit
- `-u delay` - Screen update delay 0-9, default 4
- `-C color` - Use this color for matrix (default green). Valid colors are green, red, blue, white, yellow, cyan, magenta and black.
- `-M message` - Add a message in the center of cmatrix
- `-t tty` - Set tty to use

### Interactive Keystrokes

The following keystrokes are available during execution (unavailable in -s mode):

- `a` - Toggle asynchronous scroll
- `b` - Random bold characters
- `B` - All bold characters
- `n` - Turn off bold characters
- `0-9` - Adjust update speed
- `! @ # $ % ^ & )` - Change the color of the matrix:
  - `!` - red
  - `@` - green
  - `#` - yellow
  - `$` - blue
  - `%` - magenta
  - `^` - cyan
  - `&` - white
  - `)` - black
- `q` - Quit the program

### Tips

- To get the program to look most like the movie, use: `cmatrix -lba`
- To get the program to look most like the Win/Mac screensaver, use: `cmatrix -ol`

Note: cmatrix is probably not particularly portable or efficient, but it won't hog
too much CPU time.

## Screenshots

![cmatrix screenshot](./data/img/capture_bold_font.png)

## Screencasts

![cmatrix screencast](./data/img/capture_orig.gif)

## License

This software is provided under the GNU GPL v3. [View License](./COPYING)
"
}

## Overview

CMatrix is based on the screensaver from The Matrix website. It shows text
flying in and out in a terminal like as seen in "The Matrix" movie. It can
scroll lines all at the same rate or asynchronously and at a user-defined
speed.

CMatrix is inspired from 'The Matrix' movie.

> Disclaimer: We are in no way affiliated with the movie "The Matrix", "Warner Bros" nor
any of its affiliates in any way, just fans.

## Usage

Run CMatrix with the following command:
```sh
cmatrix
```

Run with different arguments to get different effects:
```sh
cmatrix [-abBflohnsmVx] [-u update] [-C color]
```

Example:
```sh
cmatrix -ba -u 2 -C red
```

### Command-line Options

- `-a` - Asynchronous scroll
- `-b` - Bold characters on
- `-B` - All bold characters (overrides -b)
- `-f` - Force the linux $TERM type to be on
- `-l` - Linux mode (sets "matrix.fnt" font in console)
- `-o` - Use old-style scrolling
- `-c` - Only print the shadows of letters
- `-L` - Locks cmatrix, unable to quit
- `-h, -?` - Print usage and exit
- `-r` - "Rainbow" mode, rainbow colored characters
- `-k` - Every characters change
- `-n` - No bold characters (overrides -b and -B)
- `-s` - "Screensaver" mode, exits on first keystroke
- `-m` - "Lambda" mode, every character becomes a lambda
- `-x` - X window mode
- `-V` - Print version information and exit
- `-u delay` - Screen update delay 0-9, default 4
- `-C color` - Use this color for matrix (default green). Valid colors are green, red, blue, white, yellow, cyan, magenta and black.
- `-M message` - Add a message in the center of cmatrix
- `-t tty` - Set tty to use

### Interactive Keystrokes

The following keystrokes are available during execution (unavailable in -s mode):

- `a` - Toggle asynchronous scroll
- `b` - Random bold characters
- `B` - All bold characters
- `n` - Turn off bold characters
- `0-9` - Adjust update speed
- `! @ # $ % ^ & )` - Change the color of the matrix:
  - `!` - red
  - `@` - green
  - `#` - yellow
  - `$` - blue
  - `%` - magenta
  - `^` - cyan
  - `&` - white
  - `)` - black
- `q` - Quit the program

### Tips

- To get the program to look most like the movie, use: `cmatrix -lba`
- To get the program to look most like the Win/Mac screensaver, use: `cmatrix -ol`

Note: cmatrix is probably not particularly portable or efficient, but it won't hog

  "output": "#!/bin/bash
gcc -o executable cmatrix.c -lm
---
# CMatrix

Matrix-like effect in your terminal

## Overview

CMatrix is based on the screensaver from The Matrix website. It shows text
flying in and out in a terminal like as seen in "The Matrix" movie. It can
scroll lines all at the same rate or asynchronously and at a user-defined
speed.

CMatrix is inspired from 'The Matrix' movie.

> Disclaimer: We are in no way affiliated with the movie "The Matrix", "Warner Bros" nor
any of its affiliates in any way, just fans.

## Usage

Run CMatrix with the following command:
```sh
cmatrix
```

Run with different arguments to get different effects:
```sh
cmatrix [-abBflohnsmVx] [-u update] [-C color]
```

Example:
```sh
cmatrix -ba -u 2 -C red
```

### Command-line Options

- `-a` - Asynchronous scroll
- `-b` - Bold characters on
- `-B` - All bold characters (overrides -b)
- `-f` - Force the linux $TERM type to be on
- `-l` - Linux mode (sets "matrix.fnt" font in console)
- `-o` - Use old-style scrolling
- `-c` - Only print the shadows of letters
- `-L` - Locks cmatrix, unable to quit
- `-h, -?` - Print usage and exit
- `-r` - "Rainbow" mode, rainbow colored characters
- `-k` - Every characters change
- `-n` - No bold characters (overrides -b and -B)
- `-s` - "Screensaver" mode, exits on first keystroke
- `-m` - "Lambda" mode, every character becomes a lambda
- `-x` - X window mode
- `-V` - Print version information and exit
- `-u delay` - Screen update delay 0-9, default 4
- `-C color` - Use this color for matrix (default green). Valid colors are green, red, blue, white, yellow, cyan, magenta and black.
- `-M message` - Add a message in the center of cmatrix
- `-t tty` - Set tty to use

### Interactive Keystrokes

The following keystrokes are available during execution (unavailable in -s mode):

- `a` - Toggle asynchronous scroll
- `b` - Random bold characters
- `B` - All bold characters
- `n` - Turn off bold characters
- `0-9` - Adjust update speed
- `! @ # $ % ^ & )` - Change the color of the matrix:
  - `!` - red
  - `@` - green
  - `#` - yellow
  - `$` - blue
  - `%` - magenta
  - `^` - cyan
  - `&` - white
  - `)` - black
- `q` - Quit the program

### Tips

- To get the program to look most like the movie, use: `cmatrix -lba`
- To get the program to look most like the Win/Mac screensaver, use: `cmatrix -ol`

Note: cmatrix is probably not particularly portable or efficient, but it won't hog
too much CPU time.

## Screenshots

![cmatrix screenshot](./data/img/capture_bold_font.png)

## Screencasts

![cmatrix screencast](./data/img/capture_orig.gif)

## License

This software is provided under the GNU GPL v3. [View License](./COPYING)
"
}

Run CMatrix with the following command:
```sh
cmatrix
```

Run with different arguments to get different effects:
```sh
cmatrix [-abBflohnsmVx] [-u update] [-C color]
```

Example:
```sh
cmatrix -ba -u 2 -C red
```

### Command-line Options

- `-a` - Asynchronous scroll
- `-b` - Bold characters on
- `-B` - All bold characters (overrides -b)
- `-f` - Force the linux $TERM type to be on
- `-l` - Linux mode (sets "matrix.fnt" font in console)
- `-o` - Use old-style scrolling
- `-c` - Only print the shadows of letters
- `-L` - Locks cmatrix, unable to quit
- `-h, -?` - Print usage and exit
- `-r` - "Rainbow" mode, rainbow colored characters
- `-k` - Every characters change
- `-n` - No bold characters (overrides -b and -B)
- `-s` - "Screensaver" mode, exits on first keystroke
- `-m` - "Lambda" mode, every character becomes a lambda
- `-x` - X window mode
- `-V` - Print version information and exit
- `-u delay` - Screen update delay 0-9, default 4
- `-C color` - Use this color for matrix (default green). Valid colors are green, red, blue, white, yellow, cyan, magenta and black.
- `-M message` - Add a message in the center of cmatrix
- `-t tty` - Set tty to use

### Interactive Keystrokes

The following keystrokes are available during execution (unavailable in -s mode):

- `a` - Toggle asynchronous scroll
- `b` - Random bold characters
- `B` - All bold characters
- `n` - Turn off bold characters
- `0-9` - Adjust update speed
- `! @ # $ % ^ & )` - Change the color of the matrix:
  - `!` - red
  - `@` - green
  - `#` - yellow
  - `$` - blue
  - `%` - magenta
  - `^` - cyan
  - `&` - white
  - `)` - black
- `q` - Quit the program

### Tips

- To get the program to look most like the movie, use: `cmatrix -lba`
- To get the program to look most like the Win/Mac screensaver, use: `cmatrix -ol`

Note: cmatrix is probably not particularly portable or efficient, but it won't hog
too much CPU time.

Matrix-like effect in your terminal

## Overview

CMatrix is based on the screensaver from The Matrix website. It shows text
flying in and out in a terminal like as seen in "The Matrix" movie. It can

speed.

CMatrix is inspired from 'The Matrix' movie.

> Disclaimer: We are in no way affiliated with the movie "The Matrix", "Warner Bros" nor
any of its affiliates in any way, just fans.

## Usage

Run CMatrix with the following command:
```sh
cmatrix
```

Run with different arguments to get different effects:
```sh
cmatrix [-abBflohnsmVx] [-u update] [-C color]
```

Example:
```sh
cmatrix -ba -u 2 -C red
```

### Command-line Options

- `-a` - Asynchronous scroll
- `-b` - Bold characters on
- `-B` - All bold characters (overrides -b)
- `-f` - Force the linux $TERM type to be on
- `-l` - Linux mode (sets "matrix.fnt" font in console)
- `-o` - Use old-style scrolling
- `-c` - Only print the shadows of letters
- `-L` - Locks cmatrix, unable to quit
- `-h, -?` - Print usage and exit
- `-r` - "Rainbow" mode, rainbow colored characters
- `-k` - Every characters change
- `-n` - No bold characters (overrides -b and -B)
- `-s` - "Screensaver" mode, exits on first keystroke
- `-m` - "Lambda" mode, every character becomes a lambda
- `-x` - X window mode
- `-V` - Print version information and exit
- `-u delay` - Screen update delay 0-9, default 4
- `-C color` - Use this color for matrix (default green). Valid colors are green, red, blue, white, yellow, cyan, magenta and black.
- `-M message` - Add a message in the center of cmatrix
- `-t tty` - Set tty to use

### Interactive Keystrokes

The following keystrokes are available during execution (unavailable in -s mode):

- `a` - Toggle asynchronous scroll
- `b` - Random bold characters
- `B` - All bold characters
- `n` - Turn off bold characters
- `0-9` - Adjust update speed
- `! @ # $ % ^ & )` - Change the color of the matrix:
  - `!` - red
  - `@` - green
  - `#` - yellow
  - `$` - blue
  - `%` - magenta
  - `^` - cyan
  - `&` - white
  - `)` - black
- `q` - Quit the program

### Tips

- To get the program to look most like the movie, use: `cmatrix -lba`
- To get the program to look most like the Win/Mac screensaver, use: `cmatrix -ol`

Note: cmatrix is probably not particularly portable or efficient, but it won't hog
too much CPU time.

- `-M message` - Add a message in the center of cmatrix
- `-t tty` - Set tty to use

### Interactive Keystrokes

The following keystrokes are available during execution (unavailable in -s mode):

- `a` - Toggle asynchronous scroll
- `b` - Random bold characters
- `B` - All bold characters
- `n` - Turn off bold characters
- `0-9` - Adjust update speed
- `! @ # $ % ^ & )` - Change the color of the matrix:
  - `!` - red
  - `@` - green
  - `#` - yellow
  - `$` - blue
  - `%` - magenta
  - `^` - cyan
  - `&` - white
  - `)` - black
- `q` - Quit the program

### Tips

- To get the program to look most like the movie, use: `cmatrix -lba`
- To get the program to look most like the Win/Mac screensaver, use: `cmatrix -ol`

Note: cmatrix is probably not particularly portable or efficient, but it won't hog
too much CPU time.

Matrix-like effect in your terminal

## Overview

CMatrix is based on the screensaver from The Matrix website. It shows text
flying in and out in a terminal like as seen in "The Matrix" movie. It can
scroll lines all at the same rate or asynchronously and at a user-defined
speed.

CMatrix is inspired from 'The Matrix' movie.

> Disclaimer: We are in no way affiliated with the movie "The Matrix", "Warner Bros" nor
any of its affiliates in any way, just fans.

## Usage

Run CMatrix with the following command:
```sh
cmatrix
```

Run with different arguments to get different effects:
```sh
cmatrix [-abBflohnsmVx] [-u update] [-C color]
```

Example:
```sh
cmatrix -ba -u 2 -C red
```

### Command-line Options

- `-a` - Asynchronous scroll
- `-b` - Bold characters on
- `-B` - All bold characters (overrides -b)
- `-f` - Force the linux $TERM type to be on
- `-l` - Linux mode (sets "matrix.fnt" font in console)
- `-o` - Use old-style scrolling
- `-c` - Only print the shadows of letters
- `-L` - Locks cmatrix, unable to quit
- `-h, -?` - Print usage and exit
- `-r` - "Rainbow" mode, rainbow colored characters
- `-k` - Every characters change
- `-n` - No bold characters (overrides -b and -B)
- `-s` - "Screensaver" mode, exits on first keystroke
- `-m` - "Lambda" mode, every character becomes a lambda
- `-x` - X window mode
- `-V` - Print version information and exit
- `-u delay` - Screen update delay 0-9, default 4
- `-C color` - Use this color for matrix (default green). Valid colors are green, red, blue, white, yellow, cyan, magenta and black.
- `-M message` - Add a message in the center of cmatrix
- `-t tty` - Set tty to use

### Interactive Keystrokes

The following keystrokes are available during execution (unavailable in -s mode):

- `a` - Toggle asynchronous scroll
- `b` - Random bold characters
- `B` - All bold characters
- `n` - Turn off bold characters
- `0-9` - Adjust update speed
- `! @ # $ % ^ & )` - Change the color of the matrix:
  - `!` - red
  - `@` - green
  - `#` - yellow
  - `$` - blue
  - `%` - magenta
  - `^` - cyan
  - `&` - white
  - `)` - black
- `q` - Quit the program

### Tips

- To get the program to look most like the movie, use: `cmatrix -lba`
- To get the program to look most like the Win/Mac screensaver, use: `cmatrix -ol`

Note: cmatrix is probably not particularly portable or efficient, but it won't hog
too much CPU time.

## Screenshots

## Screencasts

![cmatrix screencast](./data/img/capture_orig.gif)

  "output": "# CMatrix

Matrix-like effect in your terminal

## Overview

CMatrix is based on the screensaver from The Matrix website. It shows text
flying in and out in a terminal like as seen in "The Matrix" movie. It can
scroll lines all at the same rate or asynchronously and at a user-defined
speed.

CMatrix is inspired from 'The Matrix' movie.

> Disclaimer: We are in no way affiliated with the movie "The Matrix", "Warner Bros" nor
any of its affiliates in any way, just fans.

## Usage

Run CMatrix with the following command:
```sh
cmatrix
```

Run with different arguments to get different effects:
```sh
cmatrix [-abBflohnsmVx] [-u update] [-C color]
```

Example:
```sh
cmatrix -ba -u 2 -C red
```

### Command-line Options

- `-a` - Asynchronous scroll
- `-b` - Bold characters on
- `-B` - All bold characters (overrides -b)
- `-f` - Force the linux $TERM type to be on
- `-l` - Linux mode (sets "matrix.fnt" font in console)
- `-o` - Use old-style scrolling
- `-c` - Only print the shadows of letters
- `-L` - Locks cmatrix, unable to quit
- `-h, -?` - Print usage and exit
- `-r` - "Rainbow" mode, rainbow colored characters
- `-k` - Every characters change
- `-n` - No bold characters (overrides -b and -B)
- `-s` - "Screensaver" mode, exits on first keystroke
- `-m` - "Lambda" mode, every character becomes a lambda
- `-x` - X window mode
- `-V` - Print version information and exit
- `-u delay` - Screen update delay 0-9, default 4
- `-C color` - Use this color for matrix (default green). Valid colors are green, red, blue, white, yellow, cyan, magenta and black.
- `-M message` - Add a message in the center of cmatrix
- `-t tty` - Set tty to use

### Interactive Keystrokes

The following keystrokes are available during execution (unavailable in -s mode):

- `a` - Toggle asynchronous scroll
- `b` - Random bold characters
- `B` - All bold characters
- `n` - Turn off bold characters
- `0-9` - Adjust update speed
- `! @ # $ % ^ & )` - Change the color of the matrix:
  - `!` - red
  - `@` - green
  - `#` - yellow
  - `$` - blue
  - `%` - magenta
  - `^` - cyan
  - `&` - white
  - `)` - black
- `q` - Quit the program

### Tips

- To get the program to look most like the movie, use: `cmatrix -lba`
- To get the program to look most like the Win/Mac screensaver, use: `cmatrix -ol`

Note: cmatrix is probably not particularly portable or efficient, but it won't hog
too much CPU time.

## Screenshots

![cmatrix screenshot](./data/img/capture_bold_font.png)

## Screencasts

![cmatrix screencast](./data/img/capture_orig.gif)

## License

This software is provided under the GNU GPL v3. [View License](./COPYING)
"
}

Run CMatrix with the following command:

cmatrix [-abBflohnsmVx] [-u update] [-C color]

### Command-line Options

- `-a` - Asynchronous scroll
- `-b` - Bold characters on

- `-M message` - Add a message in the center of cmatrix

  - `^` - cyan

- `q` - Quit the program

- To get the program to look most like the movie, use: `cmatrix -lba`
- To get the program to look most like the Win/Mac screensaver, use: `cmatrix -ol`
